To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mass hierarchy can be determined with 3-4 sigma significance in 3-5 years of operation of the Daya Bay reactor neutrino experiment, if a 1-2 kT mountain is located perpendicular to the reactor complex at a 44-48 km distance, and the background is sufficiently low.

1) the mass hierarchy can be determined with high significance at BaiYunZhan and nearby locations; 2) the mass hierarchy is not determined with high significance under the other mountains we consider; 3) the hierarchy can be measured with high significance if the reactors are turned off at YangJiang and TaiShan.

the hierarchy can be reliably determined in a perpendicular experiment at BaiYunZang with a baseline of 44.5km, and the hierarchy can be marginally better determined in a perpendicular detector located near the BaiMianShan or DongKeng hills with a baseline of about 50km.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a medium baseline experiment can be sensitive to the hierarchy if the background is low enough, but a long baseline experiment is preferable.
the Daya Bay experiment can be upgraded to determine the neutrino mass ordering with 3-5 sigma significance at the 10 kiloton scale, using 3-4 years of data.
the hierarchy sensitivity can reach 3 sigma in 3 years for 1-2% of the current Daya Bay exposure, with a 5 sigma sensitivity in 10 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hierarchy can be extracted with a high confidence at medium baseline reactors.
a perpendicular experiment can be designed to determine the hierarchy with a sensitivity similar to that of a parallel experiment.
